summary: This note describes the theft of the FA Cup trophy from a display in the shop window of W. Shillcock, a football fitter on Newton Row, Birmingham, after the 1894–95 Final. Police said it was taken overnight between 21:30 on Wednesday 11 September and 7:30 the next morning, together with cash from a drawer. The trophy was never recovered despite a £10 reward, and a replica made by former Aston Villa player and England international Howard Vaughton was used in its place.
one_line: Describes the 1894–95 FA Cup trophy theft from a Birmingham shop window and the replica that replaced it.
key_facts: The FA Cup Trophy was stolen from a display in the shop window of W. Shillcock after the 1894–95 FA Cup Final.
W. Shillcock was a football fitter located in Newton Row, Birmingham.
The trophy was never recovered despite a £10 reward.
According to the Police, the theft occurred sometime between 21:30 on Wednesday 11 September and 7:30 the following morning.
Cash from a drawer was also taken along with the Trophy.
The cup was replaced by a copy of the original.
The replacement copy was made by Howard Vaughton.
Howard Vaughton was a former Aston Villa player and England international.
Howard Vaughton had opened a silversmith's business after retiring from football.
